trial_court: Family Court, Shimla vide which respondent was awarded maintenance
case_name: Tikka Ram & Another vs Smt. Shanti Verma

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Shanti Verma (wife, claimant before the learned Trial Court)

facts_of_case: Claimant filed an application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. for seeking maintenance. Claimant is a legally wedded wife of respondent No.1 and mother of respondent No.2. Respondent No.1 instigated respondent No.2 not to keep the petitioner with him.

legal_principles.principle: A composite petition cannot be filed against the husband and the son.
legal_principles.held: The husband has primary liability to pay maintenance, and the liability of the son will arise when the husband is unable to pay any maintenance.
cited_cases: Raj Kumari Vs Yashodha Devi and Anr. 1978CrLJ600

legal_principles.principle: The court exercising revisional jurisdiction cannot reappreciate the facts unless there is some perversity.
legal_principles.held: It was observed: '9. So far as Issue 1 is concerned i.e. as to whether ...'
cited_cases: Manju Ram Kalita v. State of Assam, (2009) 13 SCC 330: (2010) 1 SCC (Cri) 1015: 2009 SCC OnLine SC 1214

outcome.final_order: The order dated 12.08.2021, passed by learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Shimla was set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce and child support
advising on maintenance claims under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
representing a client in a Family Court case
